chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah from Aban ibn Uthman from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who said to a man, 'Hand over to me your sheep and your camels to be with me. So if they give birth, I shall exchange for you, if you so desire, its females for its males or its males for its females.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is an abhorrent act, except if he were to exchange after what has been born and he identifies it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on conditional exchange of unborn livestock in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi addresses the permissibility of conditional exchange (mubadala) of livestock based on future offspring, a common practice in pre-Islamic and early Islamic Arabia. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that such a contract is makruh (disliked) if the animals are not yet born and unidentified, due to the element of uncertainty (gharar), but becomes permissible once the specific offspring are born and clearly designated. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on minimizing ambiguity in trade contracts to ensure fairness and prevent dispute.
